textAreas.label: t_ProcessDecisionQuestion
textAreas.text: How should rate handling appear in the journey?

textAreas.label: t_ProcessDecisionAnswer
textAreas.text: Show quoted rates, approval, and final rate confirmation as separate steps. Quoted rates may cover wages, allowances, associated billing, and funding offsets; final confirmation considers apprentice particulars such as funding eligibility and adult or junior status affecting award wage conditions.

textAreas.label: t_ProcessDecisionQuestion
textAreas.text: What should happen if the host does not accept the placement through e-signing?

textAreas.label: t_ProcessDecisionAnswer
textAreas.text: The host non-acceptance path may return to the GTO for rate or placement changes and resend for e-signing, proceed through manual host approval, or cancel the placement and have the GTO seek a new host. These are all valid outcomes.

textAreas.label: t_ProcessDecisionQuestion
textAreas.text: How should the training contract status be represented after it is lodged with DEWR?

textAreas.label: t_ProcessDecisionAnswer
textAreas.text: For this basic journey, assume the contract proceeds directly from DEWR lodging to State Training Authority notification without adding approval, query, or rejection branches.

textAreas.label: t_ProcessDecisionQuestion
textAreas.text: At what point is the host placement confirmed in the onboarding journey?

textAreas.label: t_ProcessDecisionAnswer
textAreas.text: Host placement is usually confirmed just after placement for a new apprentice, but it may be confirmed before for an existing apprentice who already has a training plan. The training plan is nominal or approximate, showing when units of competency are expected for the qualification and trade; the training provider confirms actual training days closer to delivery, usually a few weeks beforehand.

textAreas.label: t_ProcessDecisionQuestion
textAreas.text: Which roles should own the process lanes?

textAreas.label: t_ProcessDecisionAnswer
textAreas.text: The GTO / Labour Hire team owns the process lane; other parties are participants or external handoffs rather than separate process owners.

textAreas.label: t_ProcessDecisionQuestion
textAreas.text: When a host employer hands the apprentice back, what should happen next?

textAreas.label: t_ProcessDecisionAnswer
textAreas.text: When the handback is due to the host running out of work or no longer needing the apprentice, with no fault by the apprentice, the GTO reviews and places the apprentice with another host employer. The apprentice continues attending training and remains employed and paid by the GTO while a new placement is found. A disciplinary handback is a separate reason and is not part of this flow.

textAreas.label: Title
textAreas.text: Apprentice Employment, Training, and Host Placement Workflow

textAreas.label: Body
textAreas.text:
Diagram information
This diagram shows the end-to-end apprentice journey from accepting employment and completing paperwork through training contract lodgement, training-provider coordination, host placement, training scheduling, portal updates, and ongoing host feedback. The GTO/Labour Hire Team coordinates records, placements, calendars, and communications across the apprentice, provider, government authorities, and host employer.

Apprentice Onboarding and Training Coordination SOP
1. Start the apprentice onboarding process.
2. Have the apprentice accept the employment offer.
3. Schedule employment paperwork in person or online through the Applicant Tracking System.
4. Have the apprentice complete and sign the employment paperwork.
5. Have the apprentice sign the training contract and provide the required details, qualification, signature, and nominated training provider.
6. Engage the Apprentice Connect Provider.
7. Have the Apprentice Connect Provider obtain the GTO employer signature and verify the contract details.
8. Lodge the completed training contract with DEWR.
9. Have DEWR receive the training contract and notify the relevant State Training Authority.
10. Have the State Training Authority notify the nominated Training Provider.
11. Have the Training Provider prepare a nominal training plan showing the expected timing of units of competency.
12. Send the nominal training plan to the GTO/Labour Hire Team.
13. Record the nominal training plan in the CRM and apprentice record.
14. Set up the initial training schedule and calendar.
15. Determine whether the apprentice requires a new host placement.
	15.1. If yes, confirm the host placement and link it to the apprentice record.
	15.2. If no, use the existing host placement and existing training plan.
16. Publish the placement, nominal upcoming training, and progress information to the apprentice and host portals.
17. Confirm actual training days closer to delivery.
18. Update the CRM, apprentice record, and calendar with the confirmed training days.
19. Provide the apprentice with portal access to employment, HR, payroll, timesheets, training, and progress information.
20. Have the host employer view the placed apprentice, upcoming training, progress, insurance, and billing information, and provide performance feedback.
21. Complete the workflow.

Apprentice Onboarding Journey
Owner: Braden Lang
Last Updated: Sep 1, 2026
Scope: This process covers the basic apprentice onboarding journey after an employment offer is accepted: employment paperwork, training contract execution and direct DEWR-to-State Training Authority notification, nominal training-plan setup, CRM and calendar scheduling, host placement linking, later confirmation of actual training days, and portal visibility for the apprentice and host employer. It excludes later placement monitoring, host handback, re-placement, and disciplinary processes.
